newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare fall, end off on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare fall, end off on profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks pared losses at the close but still ended lower Thursday after profit-taking reversed earlier record gains.
"We saw some buying toward the close, in heavily weighted stocks such as Grupo Carso and Cifra," a trader from the BBV-Probursa brokerage said.
The leading IPC share index ended down 24.17 points, or 0.64 percent, at 3,778.46. Volume was moderate at 109 million shares traded.
The IPC notched up a new intraday record of 3,818.18 points in early trade.
Early gains came after two record closes in a row, so traders said profit-taking was almost inevitable. Nonetheless, the IPC did bottom out at 3,765.30 points 30 minutes before the close of trade.
Holding company Grupo Carso ended up 1.45 pesos (19 cents) at 47.45 pesos ($6.09), after posting what analysts termed better-then-expected 1996 operating earnings after the close on Wednesday.
Retail stock Cifra meanwhile closed down 10 centavos (1 cent) at 11.12 pesos ($1.43), but mirrored the IPC by recovering from a low of 11.04 pesos ($1.42).

The most heavily traded decliners were Telmex and financial groups GFB and Banacci, which together accounted for one-quarter of all shares traded. All three had posted strong gains in early trade before sliding on profit-taking.

Telmex L shares ended down 32 centavos (4 cents) at 15.50 pesos ($1.99), GFB B shares fell eight centavos (1 cent) to 3.21 pesos (42 cents), and Banacci B shares dropped 32 centavos (4 cents) to 18.68 pesos ($2.40).
Despite the late recovery by some stocks, technical analysts said profit-taking could coninue, as most stocks were at resistance.
"Several blue chips are looking tired. That's nothing to worry about, it just heralds more light intraday profit-taking," a technical analyst said.
"The bourse is now validating resistance at between 3,820-3,830 points," he added.
Despite falls by Banacci B class shares, traders noted that its A class shares gained 36 centavos (5 cents) to 16.50 pesos ($2.12), its second day of sharp gains in a row.
Several dealers said rumours persisted Banacci was to sell off a stake in Argentine assets. The Bear Stearns brokerage meanwhile said in a report that such a move would have its advantages.

Dealers also said media group Televisa shares, which ended off 3.20 pesos (41 cents) at 103.80 pesos ($13.31), were hit by an announcement its 66-year-old president Emilio Azcarraga Milmo had taken medical leave of absence.
Analysts also noted the bourse not only shunned another record close on Wall Street, but may even have been adversely affected by it.
"When this happens, international investors tend to switch funds from emerging markets to New York," one analyst said.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed up 60.81, or 0.87 percent, at a record 7,022.44 points.
On the broad market in Mexico, a total of 115 stocks changed hands, of which decliners outnumbered gainers by 58 to 31.

Financial group Abaco topped the sliders for the second day in a row, down eight centavos (1 cent) to 1.16 pesos (15 cents), followed by Simec, steelmaking arm of the debt-ridden Sidek group, which ended off 10 centavos (1 cent) at 1.80 pesos (23 cents).
Dealers said the gainers' list was topped by shares whose prices had moved at relatively light volume.
